analysis:
Integration across all seven source-pass analyses plus replayed source. The PR is limited to the public landing site and its docs: it removes the /developers and /contact HTML pages (landing/src/app/developers/page.tsx, contact/page.tsx), drops their footer links (Footer.tsx), repoints human-facing links to publicLinks.docs (HomeExperience.tsx line 1122, pricing/page.tsx), moves agent-document links to /developers.md and /contact.md (agent-resources.ts, pricing.ts lines 48 and 51), and removes the paths from publicPagePaths (public-site.ts line 4). The docs (landing.md, test.md, landing/README.md, changelog) describe this accurately. Browser requests to the retired paths return 404, while Markdown negotiation and explicit .md URLs stay public. The README states that format selection is not access control, so no false access-control claim is introduced.

None of A-001 to A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011 or T-041 is touched. The PR makes no change to provider code, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, the prefix cache or the fan helper. No secrets or credentials were added. Links come from repo constants with no user-controlled input, so there is no injection or open-redirect surface. The pricing Markdown still escapes model names. Public privacy text is unchanged and makes no overclaim.

Limits: proxy.ts, the sitemap generator, the llms.txt/index.md/auth.md generators and the full agent-resources.ts were not in the supplied evidence. The 404 and Markdown-negotiation behavior is asserted by docs and tests only, so it is unverified here. A gap there would affect site availability or link correctness, not a threat-model asset. The value of publicLinks.docs is also unseen, though it is a build-time constant. No security regression was identified and no threat-model update is needed.
